# Descriptive Statistics {.unnumbered}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/IBingk5fM3I >}}

## Key concepts/commands:

1.  `sum`: show descriptive statistics for quantitative variables

    ```         
    sum modrunk u_fam, detail
    ```

2.  `*` and `?`: wildcard characters

    ```         
    sum ?_*
    ```

3.  `tab modrunk`: show a frequency table

    ```         
    tab modrunk
    ```
:::


::: {.content-visible when-profile="r"}
## Model script

``` r
data <- read.csv("https://learndata.net/binge.csv")

# Descriptive statistics for quantitative variables

summary(data)
summary(data$modrunk)
summary(data$u_fam)

#install.packages("psych")  # uncomment if psych package not installed
library(psych)
describe(data)

# Frequency tables (especially useful for qualitative variables)

table(data$modrunk)
prop.table(table(data$modrunk))

table(data$sex_text)
prop.table(table(data$sex_text))
```

## Key concepts/syntax:

1.  `summary()`: show some descriptive statistics (for quantitative variables), can be used in other ways too

    ``` r
    summary(data)
    ```

2.  `describe()`: more detailed descriptive statistics for quantitative variables, using the `psych` package

    ``` r
    describe(data)
    ```

3.  `table()`: can be used to create a frequency table

    ``` r
    table(data$modrunk)
    ```

4.  `prop.table()`: can be used to convert frequencies in a table to proportions

    ``` r
    prop.table(table(data$modrunk))
    ```
:::
